item.title: Abstract Environment Render
item.description: In this 3D environment render, I explore an abstract space unconstrained by gravity or fixed orientations. The base assets were modeled in Maya, with lighting, composition, and character posing done in Blender, with assistance from my friend Yichen Huang. I also used this piece as an opportunity to experiment with volumetric fog to enhance depth and atmosphere.

item.title: Primitives Animation
item.description: As an exercise in applying the principles of animation (squash/stretch, anticipation, etc), I created this simple animated clip in Maya using basic primitive shapes. The toon shader and dreamy color palette draw inspiration from the game Monument Valley, creating a sense of tranquility.

item.title: Rigged Character Model
item.description:
I created this stylized original character to gain hands-on experience with the 3D character production pipeline. The base mesh was modeled in Maya, then transferred to Blender for sculpting, texturing, and rigging.

Multiresolution sculpting was used to refine surface details, while the Hook and Surface Deform modifiers were applied to the cloak and accessories, such as the earring, to add physics and secondary motion while being controlled by the armature.

item.title: Towne 337 Render
item.description:
As 3D modelling practice, I attempt to replicate the likeness of a photo I took of a classroom after hours. I place emphasis on recreating the atmospheric lighting created by the projector.

item.title: Warship
item.description: I love WWII naval history, so as a modeling exercise, I created an accurate base model of the WWII destroyer IJN Shimakaze using original blueprint schematics as reference. The asset was modelled for distant renders, with detail intentionally limited at the base-model level to prioritize efficiency. All modeling, texturing, lighting, and volumetrics were done in Maya.
